page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-48 is a compute-oriented virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading across dedicated allocations, complemented by 48 GB of total system memory (1.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware cache comprises 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 64838.29 and single-core reaching 2696.07, placing overall raw processing inside the top 25% of measured systems. Cryptographic and integer performance is similarly competitive, reflected by a PassMark CPU score of 51356.3 and a PassMark encryption rating of 51326.52. In application-level benchmarks, Geekbench ray tracing reached 49581.0, and small-model LLM text generation achieved 306.54 tokens per second. Memory throughput remains balanced, registering 111.99 GB/sec on large-block uncached reads and 54.44 GB/sec on writes, alongside 47.3 million Redis SET operations per second.

Because the system features an aggressive 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio, cost efficiency centers on compute-dense applications that fully saturate processor cores without demanding substantial memory allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in the low memory footprint per thread and the total reliance on external network storage. Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-48 is optimal for CPU-bound batch processing, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation pipelines, cryptographic operations, ray tracing rendering tasks, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-48 is a compute-dense instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors running the x86_64 architecture. The system configuration includes 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core, 48 GB of RAM (1 GB per vCPU), and no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. In synthetic and execution benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-quartile performance in multi-core compute, cryptographic operations, and ray tracing, backed by hardware-level AES and SHA instruction sets. System memory bandwidth remains standard at 111.99 GB/sec for sequential reads. With its low memory-to-core allocation, n2d-highcpu-48 provides an efficient platform for processor-heavy, memory-lean workflows including distributed compilation, cryptographic validation pipelines, parallel batch transcoding, and scale-out web processing.
